key_insight: The paper makes GW-BSE optical spectroscopy practical for very large systems by combining real-time propagation with atom-centered basis sets and a locally optimized real-space resolution of the identity.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the computational barrier for first-principles prediction of absorption and emission in large, disordered materials relevant to solar cells, LEDs, and other optoelectronic devices.
method: Real-time propagation of the GW-BSE equations
Atom-centered basis sets for scalable electronic-structure representation
Locally optimized real-space resolution of the identity to reduce cost
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated by calculating the absorption spectrum of a nanographene system containing 4616 atoms, with per-step cost scaling quadratically with system size.
watch_item: The approach is computationally efficient but still relies on specialized GW-BSE infrastructure and may require careful validation for different material classes and strongly disordered systems.
paper_title: Optical absorption spectra from the $GW$-Bethe-Salpeter framework for thousands of atoms
